newsitem.title: USA: Devon Energy has New Mexico gas discovery.
newsitem.headline: Devon Energy has New Mexico gas discovery.

text.p: Devon Energy Corp said Monday that initial results of a Cotton Draw Unit 76 well in southeastern New Mexico show the well tested at 9.8 million cubic feet of gas per day from the Devonian formation.
The 16,300 feet deep exploratory well was tested through a 15/64-inch choke, with flowing tubing pressure of some 5,000 pounds per square inch.

Devon said there is evidence of three additional productive zones in the well at shallower depths. However, these zones are not expected to be tested in the immediate future. Devon owns a 50 percent working interest in the well.

Initial production from the Cotton Draw Unit 76 is not expected to begin until sometime late in 1997, the company said in a statement. Devon said it will require that time to construct gathering systems and, possibly, a processing plant.

The company said it currently is drilling two additional wells on the Cotton Draw Unit. Though these wells are several miles removed from the CDU 76 discovery, these wells will test some of the shallower formations found in the CDU 76. These new wells also will test two additional zones. Results of these wells are not yet known.

The CDU covers some 20,000 acres in Lea and Eddy Counties in the far southeastern portion of New Mexico. Devon and an industry partner began their combined effort on the CDU in earnest in 1995. At that time, a 90 square mile "3-D" seismic survey was initiated. This was one of the largest such efforts onshore in the U.S. for that year. Based upon the data obtained from that effort, the CDU 76 was spudded in late 1996. The two additional wells were spudded in early 1997.
Devon is an independent energy company engaged in oil and gas property acquisition, exploration and production.
